title: Reconcile Foundation attempt resources before resumable release
description: Prerequisite production repair for task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4. Measured at delivered HEAD 3a4c30d0c1a8df0c7ba1ee363af4f094fb107e60: activation composition reaches `bindAttemptResources`, but `applyAttemptResourceReport` has zero non-test callers; `deriveReleaseTerminalEvidence` deliberately treats an absent/zero/unreconciled set as not terminal. The Foundation result path currently attempts release synchronously, while the attempt-release aggregate is single-write at expectedVersion 0, so an early DRAINING row cannot later be upgraded to RELEASED. Deliver a real authenticated adapter/reconciliation consumer for per-attempt resource reports and a strict server-owned ready/not-ready result that a later finalizer can consult before its first resumable release attempt. The caller may identify the attempt/resource and report evidence but may not assert terminality or a released state; scheduler reducers remain authoritative. NOT in scope: scheduler handoff construction, verification receipt timing, or ExpansionReleaseEvidence composition. Consumers: the post-verification release finalizer prerequisite and then task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK FIRST: at the delivered tree, prove by non-test call-site grep that activation still binds resource membership, `applyAttemptResourceReport` still lacks a real consumer, the strict terminal reader still treats absent/zero/unknown as nonterminal, and the release ledger still cannot upgrade a first DRAINING row. Also identify the real adapter/reconciliation fact source; if no production source exists, file the narrower producer task(s) and report blocked rather than accepting caller-supplied terminal truth.

A production authenticated resource reconciliation path maps confirmed adapter facts to `applyAttemptResourceReport` for the selected project/activation/attempt; durable activation and reducer output supply identity/state, and foreign, stale, duplicate, or incoherent reports write nothing.

The delivered strict readiness surface returns terminal only for a nonzero stable set whose every member is terminal by the scheduler-owned reducer result. Absent, zero, active, quarantined, unknown, unreadable, or horizon-moved resources remain UNKNOWN/not-ready with exact wrapper and source code/layer.

File-backed SQLite tests traverse the real command/handler or adapter composition (not a direct helper-only call), close before reopen on Windows, prove nonzero resource cases and races, and mutation-drill that caller state/zero membership cannot manufacture terminality and that the exact refusing layer is pinned.

Fresh daemon typecheck and focused daemon suite exit 0 with nonzero executed-test counts; explicit-pathspec commit only; the finalizer task and task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4 are recorded as consumers.
taskRails: Safety ordering: do not call resumable release before resource reconciliation is conclusively terminal; the current expectedVersion-0 release ledger would otherwise persist an un-upgradeable DRAINING row.
Use the frozen `resource.reconcile` / `resource.confirm_released` runtime vocabulary if an ingress is required; do not invent a new command kind or accept a caller-computed terminal boolean.
Exact reason code and refusing layer on all failure paths; TDD; preserve foreign work; target <=250 lines per production source and split before 400.

implementationPlan.note:
THE TWO MISSING ARMS ARE WRITTEN — and the epoch one had to be SPLIT, because one of the three values QA proposed never reaches the branch.

ARM 1, the incoherent CONFIRM: "refuses a CONFIRM that ALSO carries a disposition, and writes nothing" — sends `{...confirm("res-1"), disposition: "FAILED"}` and pins `code: RESOURCE_RECONCILE_REQUEST_MALFORMED`, `layer: DAEMON_RESOURCE_RECONCILE`, and `resourceEventCount === 1` (unchanged). Placed exactly as the rejection's issue-3 note asks: `disposition` IS in `RESOURCE_RECONCILE_PAYLOAD_KEYS`, so `checkPayload` admits the key and only `reportOf`'s coherence branch can answer.

ARM 2, the epoch: `it.each` over FRACTIONAL (1.5) and NEGATIVE (-1), same code + layer + no-write triple.

*** THE THIRD VALUE QA SUGGESTED DOES NOT REACH `reportOf`, MEASURED. *** `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 1` (9007199254740992) is refused ONE LAYER UP, at the bounded decode. I probed the response rather than inferring it:
  `{"error":{"code":"INPUT_INVALID",…,"transport":{…,"httpStatus":400}},"httpStatus":400,"ok":false,"outcome":"REFUSED","stage":"DECODE"}`
`refusalOf(answered)` is UNDEFINED for it — the reconcile seam emits a `refusal`, the decode emits `error` + `stage`, so folding this case into the `it.each` gave `AssertionError: expected undefined to match object`. That is the exact trap the rejection's issue-3 note names, arriving from a direction the note did not anticipate: not `checkPayload`'s allow-list, but the decoder below it.

So it became its OWN arm — "refuses an epoch beyond the safe-integer range EARLIER, at the bounded decode" — which pins `stage: "DECODE"`, `error.code: INPUT_INVALID`, `httpStatus: 400`, asserts `refusalOf(answered)` is undefined, and carries a comment saying WHY it is separate. That is the rail-6 answer (pin which layer answered) rather than deleting an inconvenient case, and it stops a future editor folding it back in and reading its green as coverage of `isEpoch`.
